podcast.title: Collaborations and Composer Career
podcast.body: After years working as "Wendy and Lisa" with Lisa Coleman, Melvoin returned to Prince's projects from 2004 to 2007, participating in tours and albums. She has collaborated with Rob Thomas, Madonna, Neil Finn and Campbell, Seal, and K.D. Lang, and is also an in-demand composer for TV and film, with credits on "Heroes" and "Nurse Jackie." "She's also an in-demand composer for TV and film, shows like Heroes and Nurse Jackie."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Discovery by Prince and Musical Foil
podcast.body: Prince discovered 19-year-old Wendy Melvoin and immediately recruited her for his band, Prince and The Revolution. She became an "important musical foil" for Prince, enhancing his music both in the studio and on stage. "And when he came across 19-year-old Wendy Melvoine, he knew he somehow had to have her in his band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Family Musical Legacy
podcast.body: Wendy Melvoin comes from a highly musical family: her father, Mike Melvoin, was a pianist in the legendary Wrecking Crew; her brother, Jonathan Melvoin, was a touring keyboardist for The Smashing Pumpkins before his death in 1996; and her sister, Susanna Melvoin, a singer who worked with Roger Waters and Eric Clapton and co-wrote with Madonna, was the subject of Prince's song "Nothing Compares 2 U." "Her father is pianist Mike Melvoine. He was part of the famous group of LA musicians known as The Racking Crew, who played on literally thousands of songs..."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Band Members' Marriage and Divorce
xref.body: Wendy Melvoin was a significant member of Prince's band for a period. She married her bandmate, Lisa Coleman, though their marriage later ended in divorce. Despite the dissolution of their romantic relationship, they have continued to work together as musical partners. "Wendy Melvoin was a big part of Prince's band for a while. She married bandmate Lisa Coleman. That ended in divorce, but they're still working as musical partners."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
